title: alsine arvensis
intro: Alsine arvensis, commonly known as yellow woodsorrel or bittercress, is a perennial plant in the saxifrage family that grows in woodland edges, hedgerows, and disturbed ground. It has been traditionally used for its health benefits, including reducing inflammation, acting as an antimicrobial agent, and supporting digestive health. The therapeutic actions of Alsine arvensis include its ability to stimulate the nervous system, reduce fever, and alleviate respiratory issues due to its expectorant properties. The bioactive constituents of Alsine arvensis include flavonoids, alkaloids, and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
